answer: The protocol requires each new AI agent to stake a basalt‑sized deposit of Ember tokens that is locked for a whisper‑long verification window during which the network cross‑checks the node’s proof‑of‑work fingerprint against a decentralized registry. The attacker must pay 10 Ember per identity and wait 24 hours before the deposit can be reclaimed, otherwise it is forfeited. This makes a sybil attack cost linear, e.g., 1,000 fake agents require 10,000 Ember and 24,000 hours of locked capital, rendering large‑scale impersonation economically infeasible.
